## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Load the data
# We assign column names manually since the example shows no header row
df <- read_csv("util/blimp_results.csv", 
               col_names = c("id", "model", "task", "accuracy"))

# 2. Transform to wide format
df_wide <- df %>%
  # Remove the 'id' column as it is unique per row and prevents pivoting
  select(task, model, accuracy) %>%
  # Spread the 'model' names into columns and fill with 'accuracy' values
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = accuracy)

# 3. View the reshaped data
print(df_wide)

# 4. Save the wide format for your paper/Overleaf
write_csv(df_wide, "blimp_results_wide.csv")
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(pheatmap) # You may need to install.packages("pheatmap")

# 1. Load your wide data
df_wide <- read_csv("blimp_by_epsilon.csv", col_names = c("Task", "0", "0.1", "0.5", "0.9", "1"))

# 2. Prepare the data for a heatmap
# We need a numeric matrix where the row names are the tasks
mat <- df_wide %>%
  column_to_rownames("Task") %>%
  as.matrix()

# 3. Create the Heatmap (Raw Accuracy)
pheatmap(mat, 
         # cluster_rows = FALSE,
         # cluster_cols = FALSE,
         main = "Raw BLiMP Accuracy by Model",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "orange", "red"))(100),
         display_numbers = FALSE, # Set to TRUE if you want to see the digits
         fontsize_row = 6,        # Small font so all 67 tasks fit
         cluster_cols = FALSE)    # Keep models in your specified order

# 4. THE "EXCELLENCE" HEATMAP (Z-Scores)
# This standardizes by row (task). 
# Red = Model is much better than its peers on this task.
# Blue = Model is worse than its peers.
pheatmap(mat, 
         scale = "row", 
         main = "Relative Performance (Z-Scores per Task)",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(100),
         fontsize_row = 6,
         clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean", # Groups similar linguistic tasks
         cluster_cols = FALSE)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
